name: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Dragon Gate DG-4 'Gatekeeper'
description:
A vehicle-mounted rotary railgun that fires 4mm tungsten rounds at 2,000 rounds per minute. The Dragon Gate is designed for mounting on armored personnel carriers, ground-effect vehicles, and defensive turrets, providing devastating sustained fire against both personnel and light armor.

Zheng-Dao's engineering philosophy for the DG-4 prioritized sustained fire capability over peak performance. The weapon's six-barrel rotary system distributes heat and electromagnetic stress evenly, allowing a continuous 30-second burst that fires 1,000 rounds before requiring a 10-second cooling cycle. The electromagnetic launch system eliminates the need for propellant, and the 4mm tungsten rounds are compact enough to carry in quantities that make ammunition conservation unnecessary.

The Gatekeeper has become the standard suppression system for corporate armored columns in GLMZ. When a DG-4 opens fire, the concentrated stream of hypervelocity tungsten transforms cover into concealment and concealment into nothing.
specifications: caliber: 4mm tungsten effective_range: 200-1,500 meters rate_of_fire: 2,000 rounds per minute capacity: 4,000-round hopper weight: 120 kg (weapon), 180 kg (ammunition hopper) power_source: Vehicle power bus, draws 200kW during sustained fire
tactical_use: The Gatekeeper is deployed as a vehicle weapon system for convoy escort, perimeter defense, and area denial. Its extreme rate of fire creates a physical wall of tungsten that nothing personnel-portable can survive. Vehicle commanders use the DG-4 to establish fire corridors during movement, sweeping potential ambush positions with sustained bursts that deter or destroy threats before they can engage. Against structures, the concentrated fire can breach reinforced walls within seconds.
cultural_context: The DG-4's distinctive sound — a high-pitched electromagnetic whine followed by the tearing-fabric noise of hypervelocity impacts — has become one of GLMZ's most feared sounds. Ground-level communities near corporate transit corridors have developed informal warning systems based on the sound of DG-4 fire. The weapon is so destructive that its deployment in residential areas has been condemned by humanitarian organizations that Zheng-Dao's legal team routinely ignores.
story_hooks: A DG-4 was ripped from a destroyed APC and jury-rigged for ground emplacement by a Tier 2 militia. They lack the power supply to run it at full rate, but even at quarter speed it has created an impassable killzone that corporate security cannot approach.

Zheng-Dao is developing a man-portable version of the Dragon Gate — a back-mounted system that reduces the rate of fire but allows a single operator to carry the destructive potential of a vehicle weapon. Field trials have resulted in three operator fatalities from power system failures.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutal six-barrel rotary assembly mounted on a heavy gimbal cradle. The weapon presents a predatory, forward-facing silhouette dominated by the cylindrical barrel cluster—thick, purposeful, and mechanically exposed. The overall form reads as pure industrial violence: a compact block of engineering optimized for sustained suppression rather than precision.
physical_description.dimensions: Barrel assembly: 85cm length, 32cm diameter (six-barrel cluster). Weapon mounting cradle: 120cm wide × 95cm tall × 60cm deep. Ammunition hopper: 140cm tall, cylindrical, 70cm diameter
physical_description.weight_description: Brutally heavy. The 120kg weapon assembly feels anchored—immobile without mechanical assist. The 180kg ammunition hopper exerts constant downward pressure on its mount. Requires vehicle-class power and structural integration; dead weight in any context but its intended role.
physical_description.primary_material: Chromium-molybdenum steel frame and barrel assembly. Tungsten-reinforced acceleration coils within the rotary hub. Polymer composite housing for electronics and thermal management vanes.
physical_description.finish: Industrial matte gray with thermal-reactive coating that darkens under sustained fire. Bare metal in wear spots where ammunition feed mechanisms operate. Scorch marks and micro-fractures from electromagnetic pulse cycling visible on barrel lips.
physical_description.color_scheme: Steel gray primary with gunmetal accents. Thermal indicator bands (orange, red) on the barrel cluster show heat progression. Zheng-Dao corporate yellow safety striping on the ammunition hopper and electrical connector points.
physical_description.grip_texture: Vehicle-mounted—no personal grip. Aim controls feature rubberized pressure pads for gunner's remote trigger interface. Ammunition feed handle is bare steel, scored with grip wear from loader repetition.
distinctive_features: Six parallel barrels arranged in tight cluster, each with visible cooling fins
Rotary hub bearing scars and electromagnetic coil casings
Ammunition feed system with exposed tungsten round magazine visible through transparent polymer carousel section
Thermal expansion joints visible between barrel assembly and cradle
Gimbal-mounted on heavy reciprocal dampers—designed to absorb recoil spread across vehicle chassis
Electrical connector port flush-mounted for vehicle power integration, armored against foreign objects
Mechanical ammo counter with digit readout on hopper side
Heat vents arranged radially beneath barrel cluster, darkened from repeated thermal cycling
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries corporate seal (stylized gate/archway) stamped on the cradle's right side. Serial plate mounted on the rotary hub housing. 'DRAGON GATE DG-4' embossed in Mandarin and Latin script on the left barrel shroud. 'VEHICLE MOUNT ONLY' warnings laser-etched on the ammunition hopper in three languages.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-hardened. Copper scorch marks around barrel exits from tungsten plasma residue. Ammunition carousel typically shows 60-80% fill. Structural components display micro-corrosion from thermal cycling and electromagnetic weathering. Gimbal mounts show grease accumulation and dust coating. Fully functional but perpetually battle-worn—this is a tool that lives in suppressive fire duty.
